newsitem.title: USA: American Express signs Tiger Woods.
newsitem.headline: American Express signs Tiger Woods.

text.p: American Express Co. said Monday that 21-year-old golf sensation Tiger Woods will be a worldwide spokesman for the financial services company.

Terms for the multi-year agreement were not disclosed but reports are putting the fee as high as $30 million for five years to feature Woods in advertisements for various American Express products, including its financial services and its credit cards.
As part of the deal, which has been in the works since December, American Express said it contributed $1 million to the Tiger Woods Foundation, which aims to introduce golf to inner city youngsters.

Woods joins the ranks of cellist Yo Yo Ma, puppeteer Jim Henson, the late politician Barbara Jordan, actor Karl Malden and comedian Jerry Seinfeld, all whom have starred in American Express advertising campaigns.

He has "captured the imagination of many types of consumers," Kenneth Chenault, president of American Express, said in a telephone news conference. Woods' popularity has so transcended the sport that he was dubbed by a New York Times sports columnist as "golf's Beatle."
His first assignment will be as spokesman for American Experss Financial Advisors, with advertising, using the "Do More" slogan, to begin in the third quarter of this year.
Perfect timing for Woods, Chenault said, because while he has won more than $2 million in prize money in his 10-month-old professional career, he is filing income taxes for the first time this year.
Woods, who turned professional last August, won this year's Masters Tournament with a record-breaking performance. On Sunday, Woods won the Byron Nelson Classic, his first event since the Masters.
The three-time U.S. Amateur champion collected $324,000 for his victory Sunday, pushing his career earnings past the $2 million mark faster than any golfer in history.
Chenault would not discuss the commercials. "We won't be more specific in marketing plans."

Woods' relationship with American Express is carefully orchestrated, as is just about everything so far in the golfer's professional carrer. He is handled by Mark McCormack of Cleveland's Internatinal Management Group, and is mainintaing control over his own advertising image.
"I have already established a brand plan as to who I am," Woods said, and selects to work with companies where he will be "promoted correctly ... as to how I want to be perceived."
For American Express, that image is "global."

The California native of racially mixed parentage called himself "an ethnically global person," and said he wanted to work with a global company. He already is a paid endorser for Nike Inc., Titleist golf products and Plant Hollywood's All Star Cafe.
Woods said other companies have asked him for his endorsement but he said he was concerned about how his "image is handled."
Having set ground rules, Woods reiterated that he wanted "no conflicts of interest, or even have companies promote me in the wrong fashion.
"I'd rather not be more specific in talking about the brand plan," he said when asked about other possible endorsement contracts.
"We put a moratorium out last year after I signed my three deals -- to get used to the PGA tour. I have now adjusted myself and am now seeking other opportunities," he said.
Seinfeld fans need not fear, Chenault said. Advertisements starring the commedian and sit-com star, whose romantic exploits ususally hinge on having an American Express card, will continue.
While once synonymous with credit cards, American Experss has recently been under stiff competition from other credit card issuers.
With such celebrity endorsements, American Express is seeking to boost its share of the U.S. credit market which is now about 6.4 percent, up from 6.1 percent in 1995.
American Express recently reported higher-than-expected first quarter earnings of $454 million compared with $396 million a year earlier. Revenues rose to $4.16 billion from $3.9 billion.

Earnings growth was fueled by a 21 percent increase in net income at American Express Financial and a 10 percent rise at the company's travel related services unit. The company's stock was up $1.375 at $68.75 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
